title: Patel’s book listed 60 people he labeled the “Executive Branch Deep State”
description_short: Patel’s book listed 60 people he labeled the “Executive Branch Deep State”
description_medium: Before his FBI-director confirmation, Kash Patel’s book included an appendix naming 60 people he associated with the “Executive Branch Deep State.” Roll Call reported that critics called the list an enemies list. The reporting documents Patel’s published list and the attributed criticism; it does not establish that he ordered investigations of journalists or former officials because they appeared on it.
description_long: Kash Patel’s book, Government Gangsters, included an appendix listing 60 people he characterized as members of the “Executive Branch Deep State,” according to Roll Call’s December 2024 reporting. The article says critics dubbed the list an enemies list and describes it as part of Patel’s criticism of current and former federal officials. That evidence supports a description of the book’s contents and the political controversy around them. It does not establish that Patel, before or after becoming FBI director, ordered investigations of journalists because of their reporting, or that investigations of former officials were directed because they appeared on the list. Those allegations require direct evidence about specific investigative decisions and responsible officials. Roll Call identifies FBI Director Christopher Wray, Attorney General Merrick Garland and President Joe Biden among the appendix’s names, alongside former Trump officials William Barr, John Bolton, Mark Milley and Mark Esper. It reports Patel called the “deep state” the “most dangerous threat to our democracy” and quotes him saying at an October rally in Nevada, “We are on a mission to annihilate the deep state.” Roll Call also reports critics’ concern that Patel might use FBI authority against perceived enemies if confirmed, including Sen. Richard Blumenthal’s attributed warning about potential retribution. These reported statements and concerns document rhetoric and debate during Patel’s nomination; they do not document an investigative order or prove that anyone was targeted because of the appendix.
